title: Orunmila odù record, schema version 1: DRAFT
description: The single trustworthy record of one real event. The Ọpọ́n writes one odù record per real event to a second log, hash-chained and canonically serialised like the raw log. The judge reads only this log.
$comment: brief v4 lines 285-333. Fields the brief names keep its names; `record` and `seq` are the agent's choice (the hash chain checks seq, spec/hash-chain.md), and so is `continues`, rule 2's link back (line 364), which the brief requires and names no field for (LD167). `continues`, `ceiling` and each witness's `slots` were proposed to O as Q6 and approved (2026-11-22, LD174). Phase 3 slice O1 builds the fields replay can fill from a group; net_change came with station 4 (N2), cause and attribution with station 5 (A1b); confidence and conflicts come with station 6 and are optional until then. Unknown fields are allowed (line 209).

record.description: Marks this line as an odù record, so a reader tells it from the log's header without guessing.

seq.description: The record's place in the odù log: the log's header is 0, records follow from 1.

odu_id.description: The record's id, unique in its session.

session_id.description: The session the event happened in.

parent_id.description: One command that touches many files becomes one parent odù with child odùs: a child names its parent; null for none.

children.description: A parent's child odùs, in the order they opened.

amends.description: An earlier sealed odù this one amends, when late marks arrived after sealing (station 2, rule 8); null for none.

continues.description: The odù this one continues, when the target never went quiet and the earlier one was force-settled at the ceiling (station 2, rule 2); null for none.
continues.$comment: brief v4 line 364 ("a continuation group opens and links back to it"); the field name is the agent's choice, LD153, LD167; approved by O as Q6 (LD174)

ceiling.description: True when the target never went quiet and the record was force-settled at the ceiling (station 2, rule 2); its continuation names it in `continues`.
ceiling.$comment: brief v4 line 364; the field name is the agent's (LD153); approved by O as Q6 (LD174)

state.description: open (still collecting), settled (quiet, decided), sealed (final, hashed, never changes). Only sealed records reach the judge.

target.description: The thing the event is about: usually a file path; can also be a folder, a command, a process, a claim, a turn, a tool or a network host. null when the marks behind it name no target (a gap mark), as the mark itself.
target.$comment: brief v4 lines 298, 244; null as the mark's target is (LD167)

action.description: What happened to the target. `action` takes the mark verbs.

window.description: The first and last seq of the marks behind the event.

net_change.description: Whether anything actually changed: the target's fingerprint before and after, and whether they differ. Odùs of marks that change nothing on disk leave it out: nothing on disk was meant to change, and null would mean unknown.
net_change.$comment: brief v4 lines 301-305, 381-390; station 4 (slice N2). `absent` for a known absence is the agent's (LD171), approved by O as Q8 (2026-11-22, LD174): null means unknown and nothing else (line 241), so a created file's before and a deleted file's after need a value of their own

before.description: The target's state before the event: its fingerprint at its last sealed odù, else the baseline snapshot's; `absent` when no file was there; null when unknown (no baseline, a path the baseline does not cover, a link).

after.description: The target's state after the event: the fingerprint the Opon recorded when the group settled (a `fingerprinted` mark); `absent` when no file was there; null when unknown (no fingerprint taken, or a mark came after it).

changed.description: Same fingerprint = `changed: false` (the record is still sealed and kept, just hidden from the judge's default view); different = true; null when before or after is unknown.

cause.description: The cause attribution found, by station 5's steps in order; null when nothing matches (`unexplained`).
cause.$comment: brief v4 lines 306, 392-400, 413; station 5 (slice A1b). The kinds beside the brief's `agent_tool_call`, and `also`, are the agent's proposal (LD176, Q9)

kind.description: agent_tool_call: a Glove mark of the tool call that changed the target (step 1), or, for marks that change nothing, the call's own outcome; time_match: the change fell inside that tool call's start and end (step 2); agent_command: the change happened while that agent command ran (step 3); byproduct: the path matched that entry of the byproducts list (step 4); turn: a turn's own marks; session: the session's end.
kind.$comment: brief v4 lines 306 (`agent_tool_call`), 396-399, 413; the other names are the agent's (LD176, Q9)

ref.description: What caused it: a tool call id, a turn id, a session id, or the byproducts entry that matched.

also.description: When more than one tool call or command qualified at the same step: the others, after `ref`.
also.$comment: agent's proposal (LD176, Q9): the brief's example names one cause

attribution.description: Exactly one of explained, byproduct, unexplained.

witnesses.description: The sources whose marks are behind the event.

witness_status.description: One entry for each witness, glove and sentinel, always present, plus git when Orunmila ran git for that target. A status is set only from recorded facts; Orunmila never guesses why a witness recorded nothing.

confidence.description: high, medium or low, by the rules in station 6.

conflicts.description: A list of disagreements, each naming the sources and what each said. Never dropped.

lease.description: Present from day one with `checked: false`. Ọ̀pẹ̀lẹ̀ fills it later.

mark_seqs.description: The receipt. Every odù points back to every mark behind it, so any verdict can be audited down to the raw evidence. An odù with no marks cannot exist.

status.description: saw (the witness has marks in this odù); saw_nothing (it recorded nothing, and no recorded fact gives out_of_scope or down; this does not say the witness was healthy); out_of_scope, with `scope` naming the recorded fact; down (a gap mark, a heartbeat gap or a health finding covers the window).

mark_seqs.description: That witness's own marks in this odù.

slots.description: For saw: each of its marks' key detail slots, in the order of `mark_seqs`: the mark's `seq`, and whichever of exit_status, read_kind, result, fingerprint_before and fingerprint the mark carries.
slots.$comment: brief v4 line 331 ("its verbs and key detail slots"); a field of its own beside `says`, as the example (line 310) shows verbs only; approved by O as Q6 (LD174)
